axioms: Every consumer-visible behavior must be explicit, versioned contract, never an accident of the current implementation
A plugin author should be able to code against ic without reading its source
Any consumer mutation of kernel-owned state outside the CLI corrupts the durable record
Event delivery semantics (ordering, at-least-once, replay, cursor TTL) are contract and must be documented
Machine-readable output and exit codes are contract; human-readable text is not
A contract test that cannot observe the real CLI enforces nothing
failure_mode: Did not read internal/portfolio/relay.go, internal/lock, internal/budget's reconcile path, or MIGRATION.md
Skimmed rather than exhaustively read the 5,700-line lib-interspect.sh
Dispatch auto-spawn / hook execution ordering not traced
Under-sees runtime-internal integrity failures that never surface at the CLI boundary (nil recorders, unlogged mutations)
